item.title: Oil Industry Retained Up to €200 Million of German Fuel Subsidy
item.description: Germany’s oil industry retained between €100 million and €200 million from a fuel tax reduction earlier this year that was intended to ease the impact of surging costs on motorists, a government advisory panel found.

item.title: Spain’s Joint Debt Proposal Questioned by EU’s Largest Economies
item.description: A Spanish bid to boost joint debt issuance by the European Union was met with skepticism from some of the bloc’s top economies.

item.title: Franklin’s Dudley Sees AI Infrastructure Bull Case Through 2027
item.description: Franklin Templeton’s Katrina Dudley said the bull case for infrastructure spending on artificial intelligence is winning out over bear arguments and sees the investment theme remaining durable through 2027 and potentially into the year beyond.

item.title: OpenAI Unveils ChatGPT Work Agent to Field Tasks for Hours
item.description: OpenAI is introducing a new artificial intelligence agent that’s meant to field a wider range of complex tasks for hours at a time, bolstering its push to appeal to more business professionals.

item.title: ING Weighs Venezuela Commodity Deals as Client Requests Rise
item.description: ING Groep, one of the top financiers of commodity trading, is fielding “a lot” of calls from clients to support Venezuelan natural resource deals as the country revamps exports after years of US sanctions, its new Americas commodity finance head said.

item.title: KPMG UK to Slash 200 Back Office Roles in Latest Round of Cuts
item.description: KPMG UK is cutting 10% of staff across its support teams, according to a spokesperson for the company, in the latest round of job cuts by the Big Four accountancy firm.

item.title: Wall Street Finds a New Way to Help Investors Avoid Elon Musk
item.description: For every investor who wants more Elon Musk, Wall Street increasingly has an ETF. Now it’s planning some for investors who want less.

item.title: Former Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke Joins Anthropic Oversight Trust
item.description: Former Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke has been appointed to Anthropic’s long-term benefit trust, an oversight body meant to keep the artificial intelligence company accountable to its public mission.

item.title: UK Fintech Lendable Pledges Personal Loans to Raise £500 Million
item.description: UK digital lender Lendable Ltd. is raising £500 million ($671 million) by selling securities backed by a portfolio of personal loans, a deal that would support its ambitions to push further into lending.

item.title: Poland Bought 82 Tons of Gold This Year, Central Banker Says
item.description: Poland’s central bank is buying billions of dollars worth of gold as prices dipped in recent months, according to Governor Adam Glapinski.

item.title: Corn, Soy Ease Ahead of WASDE as Traders Eye Relief From Heat
item.description: Corn and soybean futures were easing on pressure from an improving US weather outlook as traders looked ahead to the monthly WASDE supply and demand outlook due Friday.

item.title: Tech Drives US Stocks Higher as Traders Downplay Iran War Risks
item.description: US stocks rose as investors put aside concerns over the latest flare-up between the US and Iran to pile on technology stocks after recent declines spurred dip buying.

item.title: MiniMax Seeks $1.9 Billion From Share Sale, Convertible Bond
item.description: MiniMax Group Inc. is looking to raise as much as HK$14.54 billion ($1.9 billion) from selling new shares and convertible bonds, according to terms of the deals seen by Bloomberg News.

item.title: California Lawmakers Seek to Boost Reserves Ahead of Hot AI IPOs
item.description: The AI-driven stock market rally has bolstered California’s coffers, sending revenue soaring. Now lawmakers are asking voters to overhaul the state’s financial reserves to capture more of any future windfall.

item.title: Airbus Employees in Spain Go on Strike Over Working Conditions
item.description: Airbus SE employees at a major manufacturing site in Spain have gone on strike in protest of what they say are deteriorating work conditions over the past years.

item.title: Bitcoin-Backed Muni Bond Fails to Get New Hampshire Sign Off
item.description: New Hampshire’s executive council voted down a proposal to bring the first Bitcoin-backed bond to the municipal market.

item.title: US 30-Year Bond Auction Set to Draw Highest Yield in 20 Years
item.description: An auction of 30-year Treasury bonds Thursday is poised to draw the highest yield since at least 2006, underscoring how swelling bond supply is driving investors to demand higher returns from government debt.

item.title: UBS Strategists Turn Biggest European Stock Bulls With 8% Upside
item.description: Stronger earnings and a broadening rally will power European stocks to new highs this year, according to UBS Group AG strategists, who are now the biggest bulls among forecasters tracked by Bloomberg.

item.title: Africa CDC Urges Congo to Pay Striking Ebola Workers
item.description: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention is working with the Democratic Republic of Congo to speed up overdue payments to Ebola responders after strikes in the epidemic’s epicenter threatened efforts to contain what officials say is the world’s fastest-growing Ebola outbreak.

item.title: Dronemaker Helsing Alters Staff Stock Plan Before Funding Round
item.description: European defense startup Helsing has overhauled its internal share program, alienating some staff as the company finalizes its biggest funding round to date.

item.title: Egypt Holds Rates a Third Time With US-Iran Peace Push at Risk
item.description: Egypt left interest rates unchanged for a third consecutive meeting, opting for caution with a fragile US-Iran ceasefire at risk of unraveling.

item.title: Canada’s Well Health Preps C$150 Million High-Yield Bond Sale
item.description: Well Health Technologies Corp. is looking to sell C$150 million ($106 million) of high-yield bonds maturing in five years, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Senegal’s Political Rupture Raises Risk of Debt Reprofile, Says Citibank
item.description: Citigroup Inc. said the political rupture between Senegal’s president and his former premier has increased the likelihood of a debt reprofiling rather than a restructuring.

item.title: Your ETF of the Moment: Winning Big With ‘Trump Accounts’
item.description: They are reshaping stock ownership, and one exchange-traded fund in particular stands to benefit handsomely.

item.title: Altman Says OpenAI Made ‘Many Changes’ During Talks With US
item.description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman said his company made “many changes” during its discussions with the Trump administration before moving ahead with releasing its newest artificial intelligence models to the general public.

item.title: AI Firms’ Office Demand Seen Spreading Beyond NYC, San Francisco
item.description: AI-focused tech firms are stepping up searches for office space, and New York and San Francisco won’t be the only cities to benefit from their fast expansion.

item.title: ION Platform’s Bonds Get a Boost as Revenue and Profit Rises
item.description: ION Platform reported stronger earnings and lower cash payments to its parent company in the second quarter, reassuring holders of beaten-down bonds issued by the financial software provider.

item.title: TeraWulf Eyes $3.5 Billion for Anthropic-Leased Data Center
item.description: TeraWulf Inc. is preparing to raise about $3.5 billion in debt to build a data center campus in Kentucky, including its first-ever foray into the leveraged loan market.

item.title: CFTC Blocking CME Plan to Offer 24/7 Oil Futures Trading
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is blocking CME Group Inc.’s bid to start offering 24/7 trading in oil futures.

item.title: AI Training Startup Mercor Discusses $20 Billion Valuation
item.description: Mercor, a startup that helps improve artificial intelligence models with rich specialized data, is discussing raising new funds at a roughly $20 billion valuation, according to people familiar with the matter.
